name: Binohash optimisation
headline: A cheaper transaction digest for Bitcoin Script, at the same security level.
summary: Binohash lets a Bitcoin script read a digest of the transaction that spends it, with no consensus change: the spender grinds subsets of script-embedded signatures until one solves a signature-size puzzle. The published script fills the opcode budget, takes about 9 kB on chain and around 2^47 hash compressions per spend. The challenge fixes the claimed security level and asks for a better trade-off between those three.

metric.label: Bytes x opcodes x honest work

tracks.name: Standard
tracks.headline: At least 80.0 bits
tracks.summary: The level of the paper's 5-byte configuration, two rounds of 120-choose-8, as the evaluator counts it: 80.01 bits, the cap set by its 5-byte pinning puzzles.

tracks.name: High
tracks.headline: At least 88.4 bits
tracks.summary: The level of the paper's 6-byte pinning configuration, as the evaluator counts it: 88.41 bits. 6-byte pinning is needed in practice.

levels.name: Architecture
levels.description: How a round's selection is made, bound and tied to its puzzle: the primary unit of search. Each architecture keeps its own best instance.

levels.name: Instance
levels.description: One script within an architecture: its pool sizes, puzzle sizes, rounds and layout.

standard: Collision resistance under the model BH-SEC-2: the accounting of the Binohash paper with puzzle work counted exactly by the evaluator, an attacker who abandons unpromising transactions and may search part of each round, and a cap at the cost of getting around the pinning puzzles. A claimed level under stated assumptions, supported by an audit; not a proof.
rules: Only the builders under challenges/binohash/builders may change.
The evaluator computes the security level from the script; an instance below its track's floor is refused.
On every judge-chosen transaction an honest spend must verify, and no altered spend may pass without the checks the instance declares.
Recorded instances must stay byte-identical; new behaviour sits behind a new builder or build knob.
An instance is recorded if it is the first or the best of its architecture, or advances the bytes-opcodes-work front.
The judge's run on the pull request is the result; local runs are not.
Instances are specimens with public secrets and must never hold funds.

participate.title: Set up
participate.body: Python 3.10 or newer is all the evaluator needs.

participate.title: Start a submission
participate.body: Create the submission directory for a track and an architecture.
participate.command: python3 challenge.py new binohash {track} my-instance --architecture rolled-subset

participate.title: Build and check
participate.body: Build the instance and run the evaluator locally.

participate.title: Open a pull request
participate.body: The judge validates it and a bot records the row.

agentPrompt: Clone {repositoryUrl}. Read AGENTS.md, challenges/binohash/TASK.md and challenges/binohash/spec/SECURITY-MODEL.md. Work on the {track} track of the Binohash challenge: architecture first, then instance. Change only challenges/binohash/builders and your submission directory, keep every recorded instance byte-identical, argue in NOTES.md why the security level is unchanged, and open a submission pull request.
baseline: The construction of the Binohash paper (Appendix A pinning, Appendix B rounds), built with its published parameters and counted by the same evaluator as every other instance.
